title: MATH GAOKAO - 297
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.concept: Definite Integral of a Power Function
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a basic definite integral using the power rule.
questions.question: Evaluate \(\int_{0}^{1} x^2\,dx\).
questions.hint: Find an antiderivative first, then substitute the upper and lower limits.

questions.concept: Definite Integral of a Linear Function
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a definite integral of a linear expression over a closed interval.
questions.question: Evaluate \(\int_{1}^{2} 2x\,dx\).
questions.hint: Use the power rule for antiderivatives, then apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.

questions.concept: Definite Integral of a Trigonometric Function
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate the definite integral of \(\cos x\) over a standard interval.
questions.question: Evaluate \(\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \cos x\,dx\).
questions.explanation:
An antiderivative of \(\cos x\) is \(\sin x\). Therefore,
\[
\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \cos x\,dx
=\left[\sin x\right]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}
=\sin\frac{\pi}{2}-\sin 0
=1-0=1.
\]
questions.hint: Recall that the derivative of \(\sin x\) is \(\cos x\).

questions.concept: Definite Integral of an Odd Function
questions.learningObjective: Use symmetry to evaluate the definite integral of an odd function over a symmetric interval.
questions.question: Evaluate \(\int_{-1}^{1} x^3\,dx\).
questions.explanation:
The function \(f(x)=x^3\) is odd because \(f(-x)=-f(x)\). For an odd function integrated over a symmetric interval \([-a,a]\),
\[
\int_{-a}^{a} f(x)\,dx=0.
\]
Here \(a=1\), so
\[
\int_{-1}^{1} x^3\,dx=0.
\]
Direct computation also gives
\[
\left[\frac{x^4}{4}\right]_{-1}^{1}
=\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{4}=0.
\]
questions.hint: Check whether the integrand is odd and whether the interval is symmetric about the origin.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a definite integral of a polynomial by antidifferentiating term by term.
questions.question: Evaluate \(\int_{0}^{2} (3x^2+1)\,dx\).
questions.hint: Antidifferentiate each term separately, then evaluate at the upper and lower limits.

questions.concept: Definite Integral of the Reciprocal Function
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a definite integral involving \(\frac{1}{x}\) using the natural logarithm.
questions.question: Evaluate \(\int_{1}^{e} \frac{1}{x}\,dx\).
questions.explanation:
An antiderivative of \(\frac{1}{x}\) is \(\ln|x|\). Since \(x>0\) on \([1,e]\),
\[
\int_{1}^{e} \frac{1}{x}\,dx
=\left[\ln x\right]_{1}^{e}
=\ln e-\ln 1
=1-0=1.
\]
questions.hint: Use the fact that the derivative of \(\ln x\) is \(\frac{1}{x}\).

questions.concept: Definite Integral of an Exponential Function
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a definite integral of \(e^x\) over a finite interval.
questions.question: Evaluate \(\int_{0}^{1} e^x\,dx\).
questions.explanation:
The function \(e^x\) is its own antiderivative. Hence,
\[
\int_{0}^{1} e^x\,dx
=\left[e^x\right]_{0}^{1}
=e^1-e^0
=e-1.
\]

questions.concept: Definite Integral of a Sum of Powers
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a definite integral by antidifferentiating each term of a polynomial.
questions.question: Evaluate \(\int_{0}^{1} (x^3+2x)\,dx\).
questions.hint: Apply the power rule to each term before substituting the limits.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a definite integral using \(u\)-substitution and adjusted limits.
questions.question: Evaluate \(\int_{0}^{1} 2x(x^2+1)^2\,dx\).
questions.hint: Substitute \(u=x^2+1\), compute \(du\), and change the limits of integration.

questions.concept: Definite Integral of an Absolute Value Function
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a definite integral involving an absolute value by splitting the interval at the point where the expression changes sign.
questions.question: Evaluate \(\int_{0}^{2} |x-1|\,dx\).
questions.explanation:
The expression \(x-1\) changes sign at \(x=1\). Split the integral:
\[
\int_{0}^{2} |x-1|\,dx
=\int_{0}^{1} (1-x)\,dx+\int_{1}^{2} (x-1)\,dx.
\]
Compute each part:
\[
\int_{0}^{1} (1-x)\,dx
=\left[x-\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_{0}^{1}
=1-\frac{1}{2}
=\frac{1}{2},
\]
and
\[
\int_{1}^{2} (x-1)\,dx
=\left[\frac{x^2}{2}-x\right]_{1}^{2}
=(2-2)-\left(\frac{1}{2}-1\right)
=0+\frac{1}{2}
=\frac{1}{2}.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\int_{0}^{2} |x-1|\,dx=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}=1.
\]
questions.hint: Find where the expression inside the absolute value equals zero, then split the integral into two intervals.
